title: AOL Instant Messenger released
phrase: the release of AOL Instant Messenger
description: On May 1, 1997 AOL Instant Messenger (AIM) was released. It wasn't the first way to chat with friends online (ICQ) but it was extremely popular.

title: AOL Instant Messenger shut down
phrase: the shutdown of AOL Instant Messenger
description: In 2017 Verizon (having acquired AOL in 2015) discontinued AIM as a service after years of declining use. For years users had been moving to even easier to use services such as Google Chat and iMessage.

title: First message sent over ARPANET
phrase: the first message sent over ARPANET
description: A student at UCLA tried to log in to a computer at the Stanford Research Institute by typing "LOGIN." The system crashed after "LO."

title: First email sent between computers
phrase: the first email sent between two computers
description: Ray Tomlinson sent it over ARPANET and chose the @ sign to separate the user from the machine. He later said he couldn't remember what the message said, probably something like QWERTYUIOP.

title: Tim Berners-Lee proposes the World Wide Web
phrase: Tim Berners-Lee's proposal for the World Wide Web
description: His manager at CERN, Mike Sendall, called it "vague, but exciting." Berners-Lee has given the date as March 12, but he admits the document itself only says "March 1989" and that March 12 is actually his mother's birthday.

title: The World Wide Web goes public
phrase: the World Wide Web going public
description: Tim Berners-Lee posted a short summary of the project to the alt.hypertext newsgroup and invited anyone interested to join in.

title: Founding of Google
description: Larry Page and Sergey Brin incorporated Google while they were PhD students at Stanford. Its first office was their friend Susan Wojcicki's garage.

title: Wikipedia launches
description: Wikipedia started as a side project to feed draft articles into Nupedia, an encyclopedia written by experts. It quickly outgrew Nupedia, which shut down in 2003.

title: Launch of Facebook
description: It launched as TheFacebook, and at first only Harvard students could sign up.

title: First video uploaded to YouTube
phrase: the first video uploaded to YouTube
description: "Me at the zoo" is 19 seconds of co-founder Jawed Karim standing in front of the elephants at the San Diego Zoo. The cool thing about them is that they have really, really, really long trunks.

title: Twitter launches to the public
description: Its original code name was twttr, inspired by Flickr and the five-character length of American SMS short codes. Posts were limited to 140 characters until 2017.

title: Telnet developed for ARPANET
description: Telnet let you log in to a faraway computer and type on it as if you were sitting in front of it. It sends everything, usernames and passwords included, as plain text, so these days it's not recommended for anything that matters.

title: File Transfer Protocol specified
phrase: the first File Transfer Protocol specification
description: Abhay Bhushan wrote the original specification for FTP, published as RFC 114. It's older than TCP/IP, the protocols the internet runs on, and it's still around.

title: First bulletin board system (CBBS) goes online
phrase: the first bulletin board system going online
description: The Great Blizzard of 1978 snowed in Ward Christensen and Randy Suess, two Chicago computer hobbyists, and gave them the quiet time to build CBBS so hobbyists could swap messages by modem.

title: Usenet established
description: Tom Truscott and Jim Ellis of Duke University linked up with the University of North Carolina to share messages sorted into topics called newsgroups. Usenet gave us the FAQ, the flame, the sockpuppet, and spam.

title: First :-) emoticon
description: Scott Fahlman posted to a Carnegie Mellon bulletin board: "I propose that the following character sequence for joke markers: :-) Read it sideways."

title: ARPANET switches to TCP/IP
description: On this flag day, ARPANET switched from its old NCP protocol to TCP/IP all at once, with no going back. The internet still runs on TCP/IP.

title: First .com domain registered
phrase: the registration of the first .com domain
description: symbolics.com, for Symbolics, a company that made computers built to run the Lisp programming language. In 2009 the domain was sold to a domain name investment company.

title: Internet Relay Chat created
description: Jarkko Oikarinen wrote IRC at the University of Oulu in Finland to replace the chat program on the university's BBS. By the middle of 1989 there were some 40 IRC servers around the world.

title: Archie, the first internet search engine
phrase: the release of Archie, the first internet search engine
description: Alan Emtage, a postgraduate student from Barbados at McGill University in Montreal, wrote Archie to index FTP archives. The name is "archive" without the v.

title: Gopher released
description: A team at the University of Minnesota, whose mascot is the gopher, built a menu-driven way to burrow through the internet. It was an early alternative to the World Wide Web, until the university announced in 1993 that it would charge licensing fees for its server.

title: The September that never ended
phrase: the start of the Eternal September
description: Every September a wave of new college students joined Usenet and had to learn its etiquette. In September 1993, internet providers started bringing in new users all year round, and to Usenet's old-timers it felt like the September that never ended.

title: Founding of eBay
description: Pierre Omidyar started it as AuctionWeb, a hobby site. Its first sale was a broken laser pointer for $14.83, and when Omidyar checked that the buyer knew it was broken, he said, "I'm a collector of broken laser pointers."

title: Hotmail launches
description: Sabeer Bhatia and Jack Smith launched it on Independence Day to stand for freedom from email tied to your internet provider. Microsoft bought it the next year for about $400 million.

title: Gmail launches
description: Google launched it on April Fools' Day with a whole gigabyte of free storage, far more than anyone else offered. A year later, on its first birthday, Google doubled it.

title: Reddit founded
description: University of Virginia roommates Steve Huffman and Alexis Ohanian started it in Y Combinator's first class. The site looked empty at first, so they made hundreds of fake users to post from. Call it Usenet with upvotes.
